pl_marking: morphological case ending; adjective/determiner agreement; often lemma/citation form
en_strategy: subject position before finite verb; nominative pronouns he/she/they/I/we
de_strategy: nominative articles/pronouns plus subject agreement; flexible order with case marking
fr_strategy: subject position and clitic/tonic subject pronouns
es_strategy: subject agreement on verb, optional explicit subject, word order/pragmatics

pl_marking: morphological case ending; animacy/gender interactions; verb valency
en_strategy: direct object position after transitive verb; object pronouns him/her/them/me/us
fr_strategy: direct object NP after verb or object clitic position before finite verb
es_strategy: direct object NP, personal a for human/animate specific objects, clitics

pl_marking: morphological case ending; governed by many prepositions, numerals, negation, possession
en_strategy: of-phrase, possessive 's, from, some/any/no, partitive expressions; sometimes word order
de_strategy: genitive for possession/formal register; von + dative in colloquial; governed prepositions
fr_strategy: de phrase for possession/source/partitive; articles du/de la/des; negation often de
es_strategy: de phrase for possession/source/partitive; partitive/negative expressed lexically
example_en: I do not have water / I have no water.

pl_marking: morphological case ending; verb/adjective valency; recipient/beneficiary roles
de_strategy: dative articles/pronouns; indirect object; governed prepositions
fr_strategy: à phrase or indirect object clitics lui/leur
es_strategy: a/para phrase or indirect object clitics le/les
example_en: I give water to the child / I give the child water.

de_strategy: mit/durch/von/als phrases, often dative after prepositions
example_en: I write with a pen / using a pen.

pl_marking: morphological case ending; normally appears with prepositions such as w, na, o, po, przy
en_strategy: in/on/at/about/after/near phrases selected by lexical operator
de_strategy: in/an/auf/über/bei plus dative or accusative depending on static/directional role

pl_marking: morphological case ending; often proper names/animate nouns; speech act role
en_strategy: bare name/noun with comma, intonation, O/hey in marked registers
de_strategy: bare name/noun with comma/intonation; no productive vocative morphology
fr_strategy: name/noun with comma/intonation; ô in literary register
es_strategy: name/noun with comma/intonation; oye/oh in marked contexts
